subject: Civil Engineering
title: Natural Period and Resonance
description: A fast breakdown of Natural Period and Resonance for builders.

hook.text: Push a swing and let go — it oscillates at its natural frequency. Buildings do the same.

buildup.text: Every building has a natural period — the time for one full sway cycle. Taller means slower.

discovery.text: A 10-story building sways about once per second. A 40-story building takes 4 seconds.

twist.text: Resonance occurs when earthquake frequency matches the building's — amplifying shaking wildly.

climax.text: Mexico City's 1985 disaster — mid-rise buildings resonated with the soft soil's frequency.

punchline.text: When the earthquake's beat matches the building's rhythm, destruction multiplies.

quiz.question: What causes resonance in a building during an earthquake?
options: The building is too heavy for its foundation
The earthquake's frequency matches the building's natural period, amplifying motion
The building's walls crack and lose stiffness during shaking

details.summary: Every structure has a natural period, the time it takes to complete one cycle of free vibration when displaced and released. Short, stiff buildings have short periods while tall, flexible buildings have long periods.
details.whyItMatters: Resonance can amplify structural shaking by 5 to 10 times compared to ground motion alone. Avoiding resonance between soil, building, and earthquake frequency content is fundamental to earthquake-resistant design.
takeaways: Natural period increases with building height, roughly 0.1 seconds per story
Resonance amplifies motion when earthquake frequency matches structural frequency
Soft soils shift earthquake energy toward longer periods, affecting taller buildings

faq.question: Why did the 1985 Mexico City earthquake damage mid-rise buildings more than low or high-rise?
faq.answer: Lake bed sediments beneath Mexico City amplified earthquake energy at a period of about 2 seconds, matching the natural period of 6 to 15 story buildings.

faq.question: How do engineers prevent resonance in building design?
faq.answer: Engineers estimate the building's natural period and compare it to the site's predominant ground motion period. They can stiffen the structure to shorten its period, or add flexibility to lengthen it, avoiding the resonant range.
